newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's SE Prairies to see little rain to Friday.
newsitem.headline: Canada's SE Prairies to see little rain to Friday.

text.p: After a mostly dry weekend, Canada's unusually arid southeastern Prairies were forecast to see little rain until Thursday night into Friday morning, an Environment Canada meteorologist said.
"The south's been pretty dry this weekend, there was only a bit of rain but we can expect more rain later this week," meteorologist Suzanne D'Amours said in French.

Canadian Wheat Board on June 11 reduced its wheat yield outlook by 0.5 bushels an acre due to dry conditions on southeastern Prairie crops. Typical yields on Prairie wheat ranges from 30 to 32 bu/ac and were cut to 29.5 to 31.5 bu/ac.

Southeast Saskatchewan and southwestern Manitoba farmland usually produces more wheat than the Prairie average at between 32 to 35 bu/ac because droughts occur less frequently there than in southern Alberta and the land is black soil which is richer than south Alberta's brown soil, the CWB said.
Estevan, Sask., saw 13.4 mm (0.5 inch) of rain Saturday as did Brandon and Pierson in southwest Manitoba on Sunday. All other reporting stations saw no or trace amounts of rain.
"I'd be looking to see at least half an inch of rain for a breather, but it wouldn't allay any fears of drought in the long term," CWB crop surveillance director Paul Bullock said.
More rain fell on North Dakota crops, which depressed spring wheat futures on the Minneapolis Grain Exchange.

No rain was forecast for Canada's southeastern Prairies Tuesday, five mm were expected Wednesday with 10 mm forecast for Thursday night to Friday morning with another 10 mm expected on Saturday, D'Amours said.
